name: Circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders
summary: Circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders arise from misalignment between the internal clock and the desired sleep schedule. FDA-labeled drugs: modafinil and armodafinil for excessive sleepiness in shift work disorder, and tasimelteon for Non-24-hour sleep-wake disorder in adults and for nighttime sleep disturbances in Smith-Magenis syndrome. No drug is FDA-approved for delayed or advanced phase disorders or jet lag (FDA declined tasimelteon's jet lag sNDA in January 2026; a Part 12 hearing was granted but no approval has been issued). Melatonin is a dietary supplement, not an FDA-approved drug.
plainSummary: These conditions happen when your body clock is out of step with the time you need to sleep or be awake, for example with night-shift work or total blindness. A few medicines are approved, and timed light exposure and melatonin are also commonly used.

approved.indication: To improve wakefulness in adult patients with excessive sleepiness associated with shift work disorder (SWD).

dosing.start: 200 mg about 1 hour before the start of the work shift
dosing.notes: Severe hepatic impairment: half dose. Consider lower doses in older adults. Reduces hormonal contraceptive effectiveness.

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to modafinil or armodafinil
approved.plainSummary: Modafinil taken before a night shift helps shift workers with this disorder stay alert at work.

verified.note: Indication and SWD dosing checked on DailyMed. The 2004 approval year for SWD is from FDA history and was not re-checked.

approved.indication: To improve wakefulness in adult patients with excessive sleepiness associated with shift work disorder (SWD).

dosing.start: 150 mg about 1 hour before the start of the work shift
dosing.notes: Reduce dose in severe hepatic impairment. Consider lower doses in older adults.

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to modafinil or armodafinil
approved.plainSummary: Armodafinil taken before a shift helps shift workers with this disorder stay alert at work.

approved.indication: Treatment of Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder (Non-24) in adults.

dosing.start: 20 mg one hour before bedtime, at the same time every night
dosing.notes: Take without food. Effect may take weeks to months. Skip the dose if it can't be taken at about the usual time. Avoid strong CYP1A2 inhibitors (e.g., fluvoxamine) and strong CYP3A4 inducers.

approved.plainSummary: Tasimelteon acts like melatonin to reset the body clock in people, usually totally blind, whose sleep time keeps drifting later each day.

source.label: DailyMed: Hetlioz / Hetlioz LQ (tasimelteon) prescribing information

verified.note: Checked on the Vanda SPL (effective August 2026); the label lists no contraindications. Generic tasimelteon capsules (Teva, Apotex, Amneal) carry the Non-24 indication only. The CYP interaction note is from section 7 knowledge and was not re-read.

approved.indication: Treatment of nighttime sleep disturbances in Smith-Magenis syndrome (SMS): Hetlioz capsules in patients 16 years and older; Hetlioz LQ oral suspension in pediatric patients 3 to 15 years.

population.ages: Patients 3 years and older (LQ suspension for ages 3–15; capsules for 16+)

dosing.start: Ages 16+: 20 mg capsule 1 hour before bedtime. Ages 3–15: 0.7 mg/kg suspension (≤28 kg) or 20 mg (>28 kg)
dosing.notes: Capsules and LQ suspension are not substitutable. Give without food at the same time each night. Refrigerate the suspension and discard 5–8 weeks after opening.

approved.plainSummary: Tasimelteon helps children and adults with Smith-Magenis syndrome, a rare genetic condition with a reversed body clock, sleep better at night.

source.label: DailyMed: Hetlioz / Hetlioz LQ (tasimelteon) prescribing information

verified.note: SMS is not a DSM circadian diagnosis but involves an inverted melatonin rhythm, so it is listed here. Generic labels exclude the SMS indication. The 2020 approval year is from FDA history and was not re-checked.

offLabel.use: Delayed sleep-wake phase disorder; Non-24 in blind adults; irregular sleep-wake rhythm disorder in children/adolescents with neurological disorders
offLabel.notes: Melatonin is sold as a dietary supplement in the US. It is not an FDA-approved drug, and product strength and purity can vary. AASM 2015 gives weak recommendations for strategically timed melatonin in these settings. Timing relative to dim-light melatonin onset matters more than dose. AASM suggests against melatonin for older adults with dementia and irregular sleep-wake rhythm. Cautions: sleepiness, headache, and variable product content.

details.labeledFor: Melatonin is a dietary supplement in the US, not an FDA-approved drug. (Tasimelteon is the approved melatonin-receptor agonist for Non-24.)

dosing.start: 0.5–1 mg, timed relative to the target sleep time
dosing.target: 0.5–5 mg: for delayed sleep-wake phase disorder, about 3–5 hours before desired sleep onset; children with neurologic disorders 2–10 mg at bedtime
dosing.max: 10 mg (higher doses are no more effective and can linger)
dosing.notes: Timing matters more than dose; pair with morning light and a fixed schedule.

formulations: Over-the-counter tablets, capsules, gummies, liquids (0.5–10 mg; content varies)
details.plainSummary: A natural sleep hormone, taken at carefully chosen times, can shift the body clock for night owls and some blind people. Strength varies between brands.

references.label: Auger RR et al. AASM clinical practice guideline for intrinsic circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders. J Clin Sleep Med 2015

offLabel.use: Daytime sleep after night shifts (shift work disorder)
offLabel.notes: A Cochrane review found low-quality evidence for a modest increase in daytime sleep length, with no clear effect on sleep onset. It is not an FDA-approved drug, and supplement content varies. Cautions: sedation if taken before driving home, and interactions with sedatives.

details.labeledFor: Melatonin is a dietary supplement in the US, not an FDA-approved drug. (Modafinil and armodafinil are the approved options for sleepiness in shift work disorder.)

dosing.start: 1–3 mg before the planned daytime sleep
dosing.target: 3 mg before daytime sleep after a night shift
dosing.max: 5 mg; higher doses are not clearly better
dosing.notes: Avoid taking it before driving home.

formulations: Over-the-counter tablets, capsules, gummies, liquids (content varies)
warnings: May add to the effect of sedatives
details.plainSummary: Melatonin taken before daytime sleep may add a little sleep time for night-shift workers. It should not be taken before driving home.

references.label: Liira J et al. Pharmacological interventions for sleepiness and sleep disturbances caused by shift work. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2014
